title: Bumrah And Akash Deep Return To India's Test Squad For New Zealand
excerpt: The BCCI's 16-member squad restores India's first-choice pace attack, with Pant and Prasidh named subject to fitness for the November Tests.
body:
• The BCCI announced a 16-member Test squad on October 16 for the two-match series in New Zealand, recalling Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj.
  • Bumrah has not played a Test in 2026; his last appearance in whites came on the late-2025 South Africa tour.
  • Rishabh Pant and Prasidh Krishna are included subject to fitness clearance, with Dhruv Jurel the second wicketkeeper.
  • The Tests run November 19-23 in Wellington and November 27-December 1 in Christchurch, both starting 3:30 AM IST — set alarms accordingly in the US.

India have named their Test squad for the tour of New Zealand, and the headline is a pace attack restored to full strength. Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj all return to a 16-member squad announced by the BCCI on Friday, October 16, for the two-match series that begins in Wellington on November 19 — a genuinely new announcement that follows, and is distinct from, the ODI squads named for the same tour.

Bumrah's return is the most significant call. India's pace spearhead has not played a single Test this year, his last appearance in whites coming during South Africa's tour in late 2025, according to Cricbuzz's squad report. He was not part of the tour's white-ball squads, a workload decision that now reads as deliberate preparation for the red-ball leg.

Akash Deep ends a long layoff

Akash Deep returns after a lower-back injury suffered ahead of the IPL kept him out of competitive cricket for nearly eight months; he last played a Test on the 2025 England tour and featured in the Irani Cup on his way back. Kamboj, who played one Test in England in 2025 before being dropped, is also recalled. Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna retain their places, though Prasidh — recovering from a left hamstring injury sustained in an ODI against the West Indies in Guwahati — is named subject to fitness clearance.

The recalls come at a cost for others. Auqib Nabi, the Jammu and Kashmir seamer who stepped in during the Sri Lanka Tests, misses out, as do Sarfaraz Khan, Manav Suthar, Saransh Jain and Gurnoor Brar, according to the IANS report of the announcement.

Pant subject to fitness, Gill leads

Shubman Gill continues as captain with KL Rahul as his deputy. Rishabh Pant, the first-choice wicketkeeper-batter, is included subject to final fitness clearance after a left-side strain picked up leading Rest of India in the Irani Cup in Srinagar, which also ruled him out of the first two India A red-ball games against New Zealand A. Dhruv Jurel, captaining India A on the shadow tour, is the second keeper and the obvious starter if Pant does not recover in time.

The batting group is settled: Gill, Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal at the top, with Devdutt Padikkal — who scored two centuries at number three in Sri Lanka — and Sai Sudharsan, back after the toe injury that kept him out of that tour. Washington Sundar returns after missing both Sri Lanka Tests with a hamstring injury, joining Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav as the spin options, while Nitish Kumar Reddy adds seam-bowling balance. There is no room for Axar Patel.

What is at stake

India sit fifth in the World Test Championship 2025-27 standings with a points percentage of 51.52 and, on the IANS assessment, need to win their remaining games in the cycle to reach the final at The Oval next June. A two-Test series in New Zealand, where visiting pace attacks decide matches, is exactly the assignment a fit Bumrah changes. The first Test runs November 19-23 at Wellington and the second November 27-December 1 at Christchurch, starting at 3:30 AM IST — early-evening viewing the previous day in US time zones. Because the fifth ODI at Mount Maunganui ends only days before the first Test, the BCCI has named a separate squad for the tour's final two ODIs; only Nitish, Siraj and Kuldeep cross over.
